key_insight: LM-SimBench provides a unified framework, profiling dataset, and benchmark for comparing LLM training simulators and diagnosing their prediction errors.
engineering_relevance: It supports evaluation of simulation-guided parallelization choices as a lower-cost alternative to testing candidates through distributed training runs.
method: Decompose simulation into functional stages, from model compilation to schedule-level aggregation.
Profile configurations varying five parallelism dimensions and activation recomputation.
Evaluate prediction accuracy, configuration selection, and error sources using multigranularity measurements.
evidence_signal: The dataset covers 348 feasible configurations across 23 model settings from 10 dense and MoE LLM families on Ascend NPUs, with matched GPU–NPU experiments demonstrating cross-platform applicability and NPU-guided GPU configuration selection.
watch_item: Cross-platform results do not establish accuracy for every hardware or workload setting; new deployments may require additional profiling and validation.
paper_title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
